::: {.callout-note}
This report records how the European data used in TN-03 were extracted and prepared at EUROCONTROL.
It refers to EUROCONTROL systems and access arrangements that do not exist elsewhere. It documents the
processing for reproducibility; it is not part of the method proposed to the PBWG, and partners do not
need these systems to apply the method.
:::

## Data sources

| Content in TN-03 | Internal source | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flight list, ATFM delay, slot times (EOBT, COBT, AOBT), requested flight level | PRISME `FLX.FLIGHT`, `SWH_FCT.FAC_FLIGHT` via `eurocontrol::flights_tidy()` | Oracle (ROracle), account PRU_READ / PRU_DEV | Key `ID` = SAM_ID |
| Filed (Model 1) and flown (Model 3) point profiles | PRISME `FSD.ALL_FT_POINT_PROFILE` (FTFM, CTFM) via `eurocontrol::point_profiles_tidy()` | as above | CPF also used (correlated position) |
| FIR crossings, Model 1 / Model 3 | NM airspace profiles via `eurocontrol::airspace_profiles_tidy(airspace = "FIR")` | as above | FIR and UIR merged by 4-letter region |
| Regulated (Model 2) point profiles | Databricks data product `dp_all_ft_flights / output_flights` v1.0.0, column `rtfm_all_ft_pt_list` | Databricks (Collibra-registered data product) | Not loaded in PRISME (RTFM absent 2023–2026) |
| Reroute scan (Model 1 vs Model 2) | same data product (`ftfm_field15`, `rtfm_field15`, point lists) | Databricks | computed in Databricks, one row per flight |
| Ring crossings at non-European airports | OPDI flight list (OpenSky Network), `C40_*`, `C100_*` | local parquet extract (TN-01) | no 200 NM ring |
| Thai milestones | Partner contribution (THA), PBWG milestone format | file received 2026-11-09 | June–September 2025 |

## Linkage

- PRISME flights are keyed by `ID` (SAM_ID). The Databricks data product uses its own `flight_id`;
  the link is `ifps_id` = PRISME `IFPS_PLAN_ID` (unique for all sample flights).
- Latest version per flight in Databricks: highest `version_date`, then `flight_version_nr`.
- OpenSky segments are linked by ICAO 24-bit address and overlap with the NM flight window; a ring time
  is accepted only inside [AOBT − 30 min, landing + 30 min].

## Corrections applied

| Issue | Evidence | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| Databricks timestamps are local time (CEST) labelled as UTC ("Z") | `lobt`, `cobt` exactly 120 min earlier than PRISME for all 99 linked flights | +2 h (valid for summer time only; winter data need a time-zone-aware conversion) |
| Databricks `atfm_delay` in seconds | values 300, 900, 3540 vs PRISME minutes | divide by 60 |
| Databricks `pt_dist` in km | EBCI–LGAV: 2,293 vs 2,077 km great circle | not used for distances |
| PRISME timestamps without time-zone attribute | R session time zone Europe/Paris | `force_tz(UTC)` on every read |

## Extraction procedure (Databricks)

File writes are not permitted in the Databricks workspace and the result preview is limited to about
10,000 rows. Extracts were therefore run in chunks and downloaded from the result preview:

1. Model 2 points for the 611 regulated sample flights: 7 chunks of 80 flights
   (`data/tbo/databricks_rtfm_chunks.py`).
2. Reroute scan: aggregated in Databricks, one row per flight (`data/tbo/databricks_reroute_scan.py`).
3. Model 2 points for the 100-flight reroute sample (`data/tbo/databricks_reroute_showcase.py`).
4. Model 2 FIR list (`rtfm_all_ft_asp_list`, filtered to `asp_type = FIR`): 5 chunks (`data/tbo/databricks_rtfm_asp_chunks.py`), 611 flights, 4,352 FIR records.

The generated cells contain flight identifiers and are kept local (`data/tbo/`, not tracked).

## Not used

- Aireon space-based ADS-B (Hive / Cloudera): access returned HTTP 401 at the time of the analysis;
  script `python/aireon_trial.py` retained for a later trial.
- OPDI flight events: end 2025-06-13, therefore not used for the period.
